oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: gpu-7 (us-west-2) pod redwood-runtime-3c4f reported CUDA OOM during inference. Headroom metric shows ~2.1GB available. Auto-escalating to on-call. Runbook: https://go/runbooks/gpu-oom

alex: ack, I'm on it. Starting with quick checks — pod status + node usage.

jamal: grafana snapshot: headroom: 2.1GB, spare_pool: 900MB, reserved_blocks: 18 (spike at 16:42 UTC). latency p95 briefly > 1200ms for some requests. https://grafana/s/abc123

maria: container logs (tail):
```
I0316 16:42:12.123 runtime] Alloc failed: tried to allocate 2048MB, CUDA error: out of memory
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "server.py", line 412, in handle_request
    state.kv_cache.reserve(seq_len)
  File "allocator.cpp", line 88, in reserve
    throw cudA::oom;
CUDA Error: out of memory
```

alex: nvidia-smi quick dump on gpu-7:
```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 525.85.12    Driver Version: 525.85.12    CUDA Version: 12.1      |
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
| 0   A100-SXM4-40GB   On        | 00000000:00:1C.0 | N/A                  |
+----------------------+----------------+-----------------------+
| Memory-Usage:  34572 MiB / 40960 MiB                                   |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
But headroom panels show ~2.1GB free — odd.

karen: digging into allocator traces. We have a recently deployed change (shadow_reserve experimental) that moves some reserved pages into a shadow slab to speed prefetch; those blocks are not accounted in the prometheus headroom metric because headroom scrapes only live allocations. The trace shows a persistent "shadow reserve" footprint of ~6GB on gpu-7. That explains OOM despite apparent headroom.

jamal: confirmed: prometheus metric gpu_mem_headroom = total_free - live_reserved. Shadow-reserve blocks are tagged as "internal_reserved" and excluded. We see internal_reserved jumped.

alex: mitigation steps proposed: 1) drain/cordon node gpu-7 to prevent more allocation spikes; 2) force-service-fallback to q4_0 quantized model for high-throughput routes; 3) restart runtime on impacted pods with REDWOOD_DISABLE_PREFETCH=1 to avoid prefetch filling shadow reserve. Anyone object?

lisa: +1 to all. Add temporary alert for internal_reserved > 1GB so we catch earlier.

alex: executing now:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-gpu-7 -n infra
kubectl drain gpu-node-gpu-7 --ignore-daemonsets --force -n infra
kubectl -n prod set env deploy/redwood-runtime REDWOOD_DISABLE_PREFETCH=1 --all
kubectl -n prod rollout restart deploy/redwood-runtime
```

alex: drain logs: evicting 12 pods, 11 successfully evicted, 1 stuck (stateful log w/volume). Will force delete after graceful window.

maria: started a fast rollback for the heavy route to q4_0:
```
# emergency manifest override
kubectl -n prod patch route heavy-inference -p '{"spec":{"model":"redwood-base-q4_0","timeout":"10s"}}'
```
Route patched, traffic shifted to fallback region for ~95% of requests. p95 latency dropped to baseline in 3min.

support-bot: customer-impact: 7 customers experienced 500s during the 16:42-16:49 window. IDs: C-9821, C-9912, C-10022, C-10058, C-10101, C-10123, C-10200. Tickets auto-created and assigned to SRE and Support. Suggest posting status page update.

jamal: flagging root cause: shadow_reserve accounting bug + prefetch + small contiguous allocation request pattern causes fragmentation and exhaustion of usable contiguous memory despite aggregate headroom. Different from classic fragmentation: blocks exist but can't be used due to reserved shadow slabs pinned to pages.

karen: proposed short-term patch: change default of shadow_reserve from enabled -> disabled in runtime config, and update headroom exporter to include internal_reserved in available calculation until we fix the tagging. Deploying patch to canary now.

alex: canary applied to two nodes; metrics show internal_reserved drop from ~6GB to ~200MB after canary restart. No new OOMs on canary. Proceeding to rollout.

lisa: created follow-up Jira (INFRA-6420) to: 1) fix headroom exporter to include internal_reserved or expose as metric; 2) add unit test for reserve accounting; 3) audit prefetch heuristics.

alex: pushed emergency commit to ops-config repo: commit 0f9b3a1 -> flip shadow_reserve default off. PR: https://git/redwood/ops-config/pulls/87 (emergency).

maria: cleanup: force-delete stuck pod, restarted runtime, verified no OOMs on gpu-7 after full rollout.

alex: timeline note: incident opened 16:42 UTC, mitigation rolled 16:51 UTC, node drained & restart complete 17:03 UTC. Total impact window ~21 minutes.

support-bot: status page: draft posted — customers notified with initial postmortem pending.

oncall-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident marked resolved by alex. Please add any additional notes to the incident doc and schedule a 30m postmortem with infra + runtime teams.

lisa: scheduling postmortem for tomorrow 14:00 UTC. Agenda: reproduce with synthetic prefetch load, fix headroom exporter, and long-term allocator change plan.

alex: adding a note to the incident thread: consider throttling prefetch concurrency per-pod and adding a safety cap on internal_reserved until allocator changes land.

maria: will open a regression alert: reserved_blocks / internal_reserved > threshold (5GB) -> page on-call and flip a reduced-capacity fallback automatically.

alex: thanks all — excellent quick moves.

oncall-bot: Closing thread. Final labels: severity=sev2, impact=partial_degradation, root_cause=shadow_reserve_accounting + prefetch_frag.
